meta.subtitle: Integrated energy major and a net debtor; disruption-lifted 2026 earnings that consensus already fades, with the shares near their 52-week high

analystSentiment.commentary: We rate ExxonMobil **SELL** with a target range of $134 to $155. Consensus expects FY26E EPS of $11.80, far above FY25's $6.70, on the conditions the 10-Q describes for Q2'26: supply disruptions in the Middle East and global refining margins sharply above their 10-year historical range. Consensus already fades that to $10.84 in FY27E. At $161.23 the shares sit near the top of their $110.39–$176.41 52-week range. Our Base holds today's current-year multiple a year out on the FY27E estimate and lands below the price; with a Bull near the 52-week high and a Bear back at the 52-week low, the probability-weighted value sits below the price and the page derives SELL. One input decides that label: if the market a year out pays the multiple it pays today on FY27E rather than on FY26E, the call is HOLD. We call our choice a judgment and argue it in the Scenarios section. The balance sheet offers less support than the earnings suggest: ExxonMobil ended FY25 with net debt of $32.9B, up from $18.7B a year earlier, after dividends and buybacks together ran ahead of free cash flow of $23.6B.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation explores for and produces crude oil and natural gas and manufactures fuels, chemicals and specialty products. The company description names four segments, Upstream, Energy Products, Chemical Products and Specialty Products, and the company sells under the Exxon, Esso and Mobil brands. It was founded in 1870, is headquartered in Spring, Texas, and changed its name from Exxon Mobil Corporation to ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation in July 2026; the pack does not describe the corporate structure behind the rename. The revenue data in the pack carry only a consolidated total, so this report does not split revenue by business line. FY25 revenue was $332.2B ({- -5.0% -}), net income was $28.8B and diluted EPS was $6.70. The shares trade at $161.23 for a market capitalization of ~$663B on 4.11B shares, with a dividend yield of 2.60%.

thesis.label: SELL
thesis.body: Our thesis is that ExxonMobil's 2026 earnings rest on conditions the company itself places outside their historical range, and that the share price already pays for them. The 10-Q, filed in August 2026, describes supply disruptions in the Middle East, global refining capacity reductions, refining margins sharply above their 10-year range and natural gas prices above their 10-year average. Consensus EPS falls from FY26E to FY27E, so even if the estimates prove right and the market keeps today's current-year multiple, the shares are worth less a year out than today. The upside if the disruption lasts is small next to the downside if it unwinds. The business remains well governed and highly cash generative; our concern is the price, not the franchise.

catalysts: A longer disruption: if the refining and gas conditions the 10-Q describes persist through 2027, consensus would likely lift FY27E toward the FY26E level; the Bull case prices that.
Advantaged-asset growth in Permian, Guyana and LNG, plus the integrated benefits the company plans from Denbury and Pioneer; see Growth.
Structural cost savings measured against 2019, which support earnings through the cycle; the Business and moat section carries the figures.
risks: Margin reversion: refining margins sharply above their 10-year range could normalize faster than consensus models; the Bear case prices a full unwind.
Commodity exposure in both directions, as the 10-K risk factors set out; see Risks.
A net debtor paying out more than its free cash flow; the Capital allocation section carries the detail.
Energy transition and long-run demand risk; the Risks section covers the systemic exposures.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: Revenue peaked at $413.7B in FY22 and drifted lower over the next three years: $344.6B in FY23 ({- -16.7% -}), $349.6B in FY24 ({+ +1.5% +}) and $332.2B in FY25 ({- -5.0% -}). Net income fell from $55.7B in FY22 to $28.8B in FY25, and diluted EPS from $13.26 to $6.70. The trend broke in 2026. Q2'26 revenue was $116B, {+ +42.3% +} year over year, in a quarter the 10-Q describes as shaped by Middle East supply disruptions and refining margins sharply above their 10-year historical range; chemical margins improved but stayed below the bottom of theirs. The pack carries no operating-income or EBITDA line for ExxonMobil, so we read profitability through net income; the trailing-twelve-month net margin is 8.9%. Consensus sees FY26E revenue of ~$411B and EPS of $11.80, then EPS of $10.84 in FY27E. The FY26E figure is above every year since FY22, and the consensus path assumes most of it holds into FY27E. That assumption carries the valuation, as the Scenarios section explains.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: ExxonMobil is a net debtor. At FY25 year-end total debt was $43.5B against cash and short-term investments of $10.7B, for net debt of $32.9B. Debt itself has moved little over five years: $47.7B in FY21 and between $41.2B and $41.7B in FY22 through FY24, before the small FY25 rise. The swing in net debt has come from cash. Cash built to $31.5B in FY23, which brought net debt down to $10.0B, then fell to $23.0B in FY24 and to the FY25 level above, so net debt rose to $18.7B in FY24 and rose sharply again in FY25, back toward the $40.9B of FY21. Against the company's size the load is moderate: FY25 net debt is a small fraction of total equity of $266.6B and less than one year of FY25 operating cash flow. The pack has no EBITDA line, so net debt/EBITDA and interest coverage are blank, and we do not estimate them. Liquidity is adequate rather than ample: the current ratio was 1.15 at FY25 and 1.13 on a trailing basis, down from 1.48 in FY23. The pack has no mid-2026 balance sheet, so the year-end figures are the latest we have. The direction matters more than the level, and the drawdown behind it is a capital-allocation choice that the Management section discusses.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Operating cash flow was $52.0B in FY25, down from $76.8B in FY22 and $55.0B in FY24. Capital expenditure rose every year, from $12.1B in FY21 to $28.4B in FY25, so free cash flow fell from $58.4B in FY22 to $23.6B in FY25 and FCF margin from 14.1% to 7.1%. Spending is still rising in 2026: the 10-Q's non-GAAP cash capex for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $12,974M, higher than in the same period a year earlier. The trailing FCF yield is 4.6%. If consensus is right about FY26E, operating cash flow would likely rise with earnings, but the pack carries no 2026 cash-flow statement to confirm it, and the higher capex run-rate absorbs part of any gain. How the company uses its free cash flow is the subject of the Capital allocation section.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: ExxonMobil trades at a trailing P/E of 20.7x, a P/S of 1.8x and a trailing EV/EBITDA of 10.5x. The vendor's NTM P/E of 13.7x sits close to the price over FY26E EPS of $11.80, so we treat it as a current-year multiple; on FY27E EPS the multiple is ~14.9x. The FY27E multiple is the higher of the two because consensus EPS falls to $10.84 in FY27E. The gap between the trailing and forward multiples reflects consensus earnings far above trailing earnings, and those estimates rest on conditions the 10-Q places outside their 10-year range, so we do not read the forward multiples as evidence that the shares are cheap. The pack has no EBITDA line of its own, so we cite the vendor's EV/EBITDA but do not build on it. No peer multiples were captured, so we do not benchmark ExxonMobil against other integrated majors. The Street's targets run from $142.00 to $200.00, with a consensus of $171.91 and a median of $173.50, and 10 of 25 analysts rate the shares Buy and 15 Hold. We do not adopt the consensus target as our Base, because the pack does not show the estimate or multiple behind it.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: The Middle East disruption and tight refining capacity last through 2027, and consensus lifts FY27E toward the FY26E EPS of $11.80. The market keeps paying the ~14.9x it pays today on FY27E, now on the FY26E level of earnings, which gives $175.82, close to the 52-week high of $176.41. We assume no higher multiple on earnings the 10-Q ties to conditions outside their historical range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Consensus is right: a year out, FY27E EPS of $10.84 is the current-year figure. Refining margins ease from their above-range level but the disruption does not fully unwind. The market keeps paying the 13.7x current-year multiple it pays today on FY26E, which gives $148.51.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: The supply disruption resolves and refining margins return to their 10-year range within the year, so the market values the shares on earnings near FY25's $6.70. The shares return to the 52-week low of $110.39, a multiple of FY25 EPS between today's forward and trailing multiples. The fall comes from earnings, not from a lower multiple, and we do not deepen it for net debt, because a P/E-based price is already after finance costs.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We weight the Base at 55%, the Bull at 25% and the Bear at 20%. The weighted fair value of $147.71 sits below the $161.23 price, the Bear sits about a third below it, and the page derives SELL. The Base multiple decides the label. For holding today's current-year multiple a year out: the market already discounts earnings it treats as elevated, and a year from now the consensus path still points down, so the same discount should apply to FY27E. Against it: falling cyclical earnings often earn a higher multiple, and the trailing P/E shows the market paying more per dollar of lower earnings today. If the market a year out paid on FY27E the multiple it pays on that estimate today, the Base would sit at roughly today's price and the label would derive HOLD. We hold the current-year multiple because the 10-Q describes the conditions behind the earnings as outside their historical range; that is a judgment, and the call is close on this one input. The weights matter less: only a shift of more than ten points from Bear to Bull derives HOLD. We keep the Bear to a fifth of the weight because a full unwind within a year needs both the gas disruption, which the 10-Q calls ongoing, and refining capacity to normalize. The price history frames the Bear: the shares have risen sharply from the 52-week low and sit not far below the high. The page's recent closes hold in a narrow band near today's price, so the rise came earlier; no source dates or explains it, and we do not assign it a cause.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The pack's revenue data carry ExxonMobil as a single consolidated segment, with FY25 revenue of $332.2B, while the company description and the 10-Q's cash-capex table name four segments. We use the consolidated revenue figure and do not assign revenue to individual lines. The four businesses are Upstream (crude oil and natural gas), Energy Products (fuels, aromatics and catalysts, plus licensing), Chemical Products (olefins, polyolefins and intermediates) and Specialty Products (lubricants, basestocks, waxes, synthetics, elastomers and resins). The 10-Q's cash-capex table shows where capital goes: of $6,787M of total cash capex in Q2'26, Upstream took $5,852M, Energy Products $527M, Chemical Products $307M, Specialty Products $11M and Other $90M. Upstream dominates investment, and management groups its growth around advantaged assets: Permian, Guyana and LNG.

moatFactors.name: Advantaged assets
moatFactors.body: ExxonMobil concentrates investment in what it calls advantaged assets, Permian, Guyana and LNG, and in advantaged projects it describes as delivering higher than average returns. Most of the company's cash capex goes to Upstream, which builds the resource base behind those assets. The advantage is real but cyclical: its value rises and falls with commodity prices.

moatFactors.name: Integration
moatFactors.body: The company spans exploration and production through fuels, chemicals and specialty products under the Exxon, Esso and Mobil brands. The 10-K warns that a material decline in oil or gas prices could hurt Upstream most, while a material increase could hurt Energy Products, Chemical Products and Specialty Products most. Holding both sides may soften the swing in either direction, though the 2026 results show earnings can still move sharply.

moatFactors.name: Structural cost discipline
moatFactors.body: The 10-Q puts cumulative Structural Cost Savings at $16.3B relative to 2019, including $1.2B added in the six months ended June 30, 2026. Sustained cost reduction supports through-cycle margins. The measure is a company-defined non-GAAP figure set against a 2019 base, and the company notes the estimates may be revised if prior reductions prove unsustainable.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat narrow. Advantaged assets, integration and cost discipline are genuine, but the business is a commodity business, as the 10-K's risk factors say directly, and returns follow prices and margins the company does not set. The 10-K also describes long-run threats from energy efficiency, alternative energy and shifting consumer preferences. The lower-emission ventures the company lists, from carbon capture and hydrogen to lithium and low-carbon data centers, depend on supportive policy and technology by the company's own account, so they do not yet widen the moat. The net-zero ambitions for operated assets by 2050, and for integrated Upstream Permian Basin unconventional operated assets by 2035, frame a long transition rather than a near-term earnings driver.

points: Advantaged assets, Permian, Guyana and LNG, are the company's identified growth engines, and most of its cash capex goes to Upstream; the Business and moat section carries the capex split.

Consensus sees FY26E revenue of ~$411B, up {+ +24% +} on FY25. The pack does not split that rise into price and volume, and the 10-Q frames the period around supply disruptions and refining capacity reductions, so we treat it as cyclical rather than structural; consensus EPS steps down in FY27E.
The 10-Q lists the integrated benefits the company plans from Denbury and Pioneer among its forward-looking statements; the pack gives no figure for them.
Structural cost savings are a lever on through-cycle earnings even without top-line growth; the moat section quantifies them.

Lower-emission ventures, including carbon capture and storage, hydrogen, lithium and lower-emission fuels, are long-term options that the company says depend on policy support and technological progress.

management.leadership: The pack includes no executive-officer roster, so we do not name individual managers. The 2026 proxy statement, filed in April 2026, describes a largely refreshed board: nearly 70% of directors have joined since 2021, and the average independent-director tenure is 4.6 years, which the company presents as balancing continuity with fresh perspective. The board lists capital discipline, portfolio optimization, risk management and safety, long-cycle investment stewardship and shareholder engagement as its oversight priorities. A proxy footnote claims leading earnings ex. identified items and cash-flow-from-operations growth versus each of the other IOCs from 2019 to 2025; if accurate, that points to sound execution through a volatile cycle, but it is the company's own comparison.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation favors shareholder returns and Upstream investment, and in the last two years returns have outrun free cash flow. In FY25 the company paid $17.2B in dividends, which the proxy says ranked second among all S&P 500 companies per Bloomberg data. It also repurchased $20.3B of stock. Together those payouts exceeded FY25 free cash flow, as they did in FY24; from FY21 through FY23 free cash flow covered both. The shortfall shows up on the balance sheet, where cash fell and net debt rose, as the Financials section sets out. Dividends alone sit within free cash flow, so the buyback is the flexible part of the program. Capex has risen every year since FY21's $12.1B, concentrated in Upstream. In our view the current buyback pace depends on the 2026 earnings strength lasting: if margins revert, either buybacks slow or net debt keeps rising. We would expect the buyback to give way first, though the company has not said so.
management.governance: Governance scores well on independence. The 2026 proxy statement, filed in April 2026, reports that 12 of 13 directors are independent, that 100% of the Audit, Compensation, Nominating and Governance, and Environment, Safety and Public Policy committee members are independent, and that a Lead Independent Director holds defined authorities. Shareholders were asked to ratify PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as auditor for 2026 and to cast an advisory say-on-pay vote. The proxy also asked them to approve redomiciling the company from New Jersey to Texas, its headquarters state; the board said shareholder rights remain largely comparable and that it is not adopting elective Texas provisions that weaken them. The pack does not report the vote results. Related-person transactions fall under written guidelines overseen by the Nominating and Governance Committee. The pack carries no executive-pay amounts or insider-ownership figures, so we do not assess them.

idiosyncratic: Earnings fade faster than consensus. The FY27E estimate assumes most of the 2026 strength holds, but the 10-Q ties that strength to global refining capacity reductions and to supply disruptions, conditions that can reverse within a year. With the shares near their 52-week high, a faster fade would reach the price quickly; the Bear case prices a full unwind.

Commodity sensitivity in both directions. The 10-K states that a material decline in oil or natural gas prices could have a material adverse effect, especially in Upstream, while a material increase could hurt Energy Products, Chemical Products and Specialty Products.

Chemical weakness. The 10-Q says chemical margins improved but remained below the bottom of their 10-year range, with regional supply constraints affecting product availability, particularly in Asia; a longer stretch at those levels would weigh on the non-Upstream businesses.

Less balance-sheet room if the cycle turns. Net debt already rose in FY25 while payouts exceeded free cash flow, so a downturn would push it higher unless buybacks slow. The load is moderate against equity, so we see this as a limit on shareholder returns rather than a solvency risk.
risks.systemic: ExxonMobil faces the broad forces that move every oil, gas and petrochemical producer. Demand tracks global economic activity, so recessions or slow growth reduce results directly, per the 10-K. Supply depends on OPEC and OPEC+ production quotas, government policies that restrict or expand oil and gas production, and wars or other disruptions to transport routes. Interest rates, inflation and currency movements affect costs and demand. Over the long run, efficiency gains, alternative energy and changing consumer preferences could erode demand for the company's core products. None of these is specific to ExxonMobil, but its earnings follow commodity prices and margins, so they reach its results directly.

body: Our recommendation is SELL, with a target range of $134 to $155 around a Base implied price of $148.51. ExxonMobil is a well-governed, cash-generative major, and we are not calling the business impaired. Our view is that the price already pays for 2026 earnings that rest on conditions outside their historical range, while the company carries net debt of $32.9B and pays out more than its free cash flow. The call depends on holding today's current-year multiple a year out, which the Scenarios section argues from both sides.

On unchanged scenarios the label moves with the price: at or below the top of our range the page derives HOLD, and at the bottom of the range it derives BUY. Away from price, we would move to HOLD if consensus lifts FY27E EPS toward the FY26E level of $11.80 while the conditions the 10-Q describes persist, because that would carry our Base to about today's price.
